author: max51527
body:
## Summary

Found during a pre-launch hardening pass. The newsletter signup endpoint (`/api/newsletter-subscribe`) has a **broken IP rate-limit**: it's a no-op, leaving a public, Turnstile-less endpoint open to spam inserts.

### The bug

`handleNewsletterSubscribe` computes `ipHash = sha256(ip)`, then:
- rate-limit query: `SELECT COUNT(*) ... WHERE source = ?` bound to `ipHash`
- INSERT: stores `source` = the real source string (`'home'`, etc.) and **never persists the ipHash anywhere**

So the query checks `source = <a sha256 hash>` against rows where `source = 'home'` → never matches → counter is always 0 → the per-IP limit never triggers.

### The fix

- Add `ip_hash` column to `email_captures` (+ `idx_email_captures_ip` index) in `schema.sql`
- Persist `ip_hash` on INSERT; rate-limit on `ip_hash`
- `deploy.yml` now applies `schema.sql` (covers fresh DBs) **and** runs a guarded `ALTER TABLE email_captures ADD COLUMN ip_hash TEXT || true` so the **existing prod table** (created earlier without the column) gets it *before* the worker rolls out — otherwise the first post-deploy signup would 500 with `no such column: ip_hash`.

Both migration commands are idempotent and safe to re-run on every deploy.

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge → run `deploy.yml` → migration step succeeds (creates column on existing DB)
- [ ] `POST /api/newsletter-subscribe` with a valid email → 200, row in `email_captures` with `ip_hash` populated
- [ ] Hammer >10 times from same IP within an hour → 11th returns HTTP 429
- [ ] Re-run `deploy.yml` → ALTER step hits "duplicate column", swallowed by `|| true`, job stays green

author: aviezerl
body:
Addresses inefficiencies, optimizations, and bugs found in a package review. Each fix is a separate commit. All 299 tests pass (`devtools::test()`, `NOT_CRAN=true`), and `R CMD INSTALL` is clean.

## Performance (behavior-preserving, verified against regression snapshots)

- **Drop the dense `k × n` vote matrix in `ReassignWorker`.** Each `parallelReduce` split copy allocated a `centers × observations` matrix, and `join()`/`apply_votes()` were `O(k·n)` - per-iteration memory and time scaled with `k`. The assignment vector is already shared by reference and written in place over disjoint chunks, so the matrix was redundant. Now only a scalar change counter is merged, and votes are applied in one `O(n)` pass in ascending index order, keeping per-center accumulation (hence results) bit-identical. Verified under 1 and 4 threads.
- **Spearman distance no longer computes a discarded p-value.** `dist()` evaluated an incomplete-beta p-value (`betai`, up to 100 continued-fraction iterations) on every point-to-center comparison and threw it away. Removed. Also swapped the per-call `std::list` + `list::sort` for a reusable `thread_local std::vector` + `std::sort`, and dropped a center-rank precompute that `dist()` never read. Tie handling in `cond_mid_ranking` makes ranks independent of the unstable sort, so results are unchanged.
- **`predict_tgl_kmeans()` chunk size.** Each chunk built a full `(chunk + centers)²` matrix but used only the `obs × centers` block. Since every value is pairwise (chunk-independent), lowering the chunk from 10000 to 1000 cuts the discarded `O(chunk²)` work ~10× on large inputs with identical results.
- Avoid per-line `std::endl` flushes in the C++ progress output.

## Bug fixes

- **Intra-cluster ordering (`hclust_intra_clusters = TRUE`).** `intra_clust_order` was set to `hc$order` (dendrogram-position → observation) and then sorted by, producing a scrambled order. The correct mapping is the inverse permutation `order(hc$order)`. Added a regression test comparing the within-cluster order to `ids[hc$order]`.
- **`match_clusters()`** relied on `$` partial matching of `res$clust` → `res$cluster`; now references `res$cluster` directly (and silences the `summarise()` grouping message).

## Cleanup

- Removed dead code: `reduce_coclust`/`reduce_num_trials` (compiled and exported via Rcpp but never referenced from R), the unused `wilcoxon_rank_sum`/`siegel_tukey` templates, and the now-orphaned `corr_pv`/`betai`/`betacf`/`dbl_gamma_ln` p-value helpers. Regenerated the Rcpp bindings.
- Documented the Pearson distance's NA approximation (precomputed center moments are exact without NAs; recomputing per pair would slow the hot loop - left as an intentional tradeoff).

## ⚠️ Behavior change (isolated commit - drop if undesired)

- **`downsample_matrix()` per-column seeding.** Columns derived their RNG seed as `random_seed + col`, feeding `std::minstd_rand` consecutive seeds whose low-order LCG output is correlated across adjacent columns. Replaced with a SplitMix mix of `(seed, col)`. Output stays fully deterministic per `(seed, matrix)` but **differs from prior versions** - relevant for anyone relying on cross-version reproducibility. Kept as its own commit (`Decorrelate per-column downsampling seeds`) so it can be reverted independently.

## Notes

- Spearman regression cases were added to `test-regression.R` (no-NA and with-NA paths). The `.rds` snapshots live in the gitignored, external `TGLKMEANS_REGRESSION_DIR` like the existing euclid/pearson ones; they were generated locally from the pre-change code and confirmed to still match.

### Motivation
- Persist MemoryManager state (providers, buckets, chunk locations, and health) to disk so metadata survives restarts.  
- Reconstruct in-memory bucket hierarchy, vector contents, and provider objects during startup from a versioned manifest.  
- Avoid crashing on corrupted or partially-missing data by marking affected chunks unhealthy and continuing to operate.

### Description
- Add a versioned `manifest.json` format and manifest types under `MemoryManager.basePath` that record providers, bucket configs/hierarchy, chunk IDs, chunk locations, and unhealthy chunk reasons.  
- Persist the manifest after provider additions/removals, bucket creation/removal, and chunk storage using queued background saves and atomic temp-file renames in `src/core/MemoryManager.ts`.  
- Load and restore providers, root buckets, sub-buckets, vector contents, and chunk locations in `MemoryManager.initialize`, and mark missing/unreadable chunks as unhealthy instead of throwing.  
- Add hooks and accessors required for persistence: bucket change callback and `getConfig`/`getChunks` in `src/core/Bucket.ts`, `getChunks` in `src/core/VectorStore.ts`, and local-provider metadata accessors in `src/providers/LocalStorageProvider.ts`.

body:
## What

`ProvenanceBuffer` was hoisted into the flat crate namespace but had no consumer outside `rimap-audit`. Delete that re-export and demote the type to `pub(crate)`.

`TrailingState` / `current_inode` / `read_trailing_state` (the next re-export line) are **kept** — they are load-bearing for the boot path (`boot/audit_init.rs`) and the `audit_merge` integration test.

## Note on the dead_code expectation

Removing the re-export unmasks that `ProvenanceBuffer` is unwired scaffolding — its `fetch_message` / `search` feeders land in a future sprint (see the module doc), and today it is exercised **only by its own tests**. So demoting alone trips `dead_code` under `-D warnings` (verified: 7 warnings).

The issue's literal recommendation (demote to `pub(crate)`) therefore needed one addition to compile. Rather than delete the planned scaffolding, I scoped a `dead_code` expectation to non-test builds:

```rust
#![cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code, reason = "feeders wired in a future sprint; see module doc"))]
```

This is clean in both compilation configs, and when the feeders are wired (non-test usage appears) the expectation becomes unfulfilled and prompts the suppression's removal. `#[expect]` is the clippy-sanctioned form (`allow_attributes = deny` forbids only `#[allow]`).

Verified: `cargo clippy -p rimap-audit --all-targets --all-features` and lib-only clippy both clean; 154 audit tests pass.

Closes #348

web annotation systems (Hypothesis, Utterances, Giscus), forcing users to add
`validate-yaml: false` to suppress the YAML validation error. This disables
schema validation project-wide, which is a poor workaround.

Closes #6.

## Solution

Scope the extension configuration under `extensions.quarto-comments`, following
the namespace convention recommended by the Quarto team. Quarto already accepts
arbitrary sub-keys under `extensions.<name>`, so no YAML validation override
is needed.

Discussed upstream with the Quarto team:
https://github.com/orgs/quarto-dev/discussions/14556

## Changes

- `comment_core.lua`: read config from `meta.extensions["quarto-comments"]`
  instead of `meta.comments`
- `example.qmd`: move config block from `comments:` to
  `extensions.quarto-comments:`, remove `validate-yaml: false`
- `README.md`: update configuration example accordingly

## Breaking change

Users upgrading from a previous version must rename the configuration key
in their document front matter from `comments:` to
`extensions.quarto-comments:` and remove `validate-yaml: false`.

author: jeffreydissmann
body:
## The bug

After 2026.05.04 (consolidated HomeBox + Caddy fixes), submitting the login form on any deployment behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy does *nothing visible*: the user stays on `/login` with no flash message, no validation error, no banner. The form looks broken.

## Root cause

Captured via browser devtools:

```
POST  https://example.test/login    → 503
GET   http://example.test/dashboard  ← redirect target (note the http:// scheme)
Console: AxiosError: Network Error
```

`bootstrap/app.php` never called `->trustProxies(at: '*')`. Without it Laravel ignores `X-Forwarded-Proto` from the proxy and sees the request as plain HTTP:

- `request()->isSecure()` is false
- `route()` / `redirect()->intended()` generate `http://…` URLs
- Server returns a 302 with `Location: http://…/dashboard`
- The browser refuses to follow it as an Inertia XHR from an `https://` origin (mixed content)
- Inertia surfaces only "Network Error" — no useful UI

Identical pattern would break every other authenticated redirect (logout, post-create redirects, etc.).

## Fix

One-liner in `bootstrap/app.php`: `\$middleware->trustProxies(at: '*')`. Stockroom is self-hosted on arbitrary networks, so the proxy IP range is not known up-front; trusting any proxy is the right default. Users who want to lock this down can change the `at:` list locally — worth a future docs note.

## Test

New `test_redirects_respect_x_forwarded_proto_from_reverse_proxy` in `AuthenticationTest` issues a request with `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` and asserts `request()->isSecure()` is true and `url()->current()` starts with `https://`. Without the fix this fails.

```
Tests:    5 passed (11 assertions)
```

## Deployment

This should ship as **2026.05.05** today — login is broken on every reverse-proxy deploy that came after 2026.05.04.

author: marciano147
body:
**Stacked on PR #131 (C7)** — merge that first.

After shipping C1–C7 I pressure-tested the dual-mode prefund strategy layer by layer. Three real issues, all fixed in this PR.

## L-PR-1 (critical): funded orders past CLTV stayed matchable

A \`funded\` or \`partially_swept\` order whose \`prefundRefundEligibleAfterUnixTime\` had passed remained in the order book. If a taker matched at the same moment the maker broadcast a CLTV refund tx, both txs raced for the same prefund UTXO. The loser left an orphan sweep row stuck in \`pending\` forever. The C3 observer only auto-expired \`pending_funding\` orders.

**Fix:** new \`OtcTradeService.runPrefundCltvCutoffIteration\` scans \`funded\` + \`partially_swept\` orders past CLTV and flips \`order.status\` to \`'cancelled'\`. \`prefund_state\` stays so the maker can still call \`requestPrefundRefund\`. Order vanishes from the book; the refund path stays open. Wired via new repository method \`cancelOrderForCltvCutoff\` (Pg + InMemory) with a guarded UPDATE.

## L-PR-2 (critical): refund PSBT referenced the original funding outpoint

\`requestPrefundRefund\` passed \`order\` to the \`PrefundRefundPsbtBuilder\`, which contains the **original** \`prefundFundedOutpoint\`. After any sweep, that outpoint is spent. The refund PSBT would reference a spent input and fail at broadcast.

**Fix:** \`PrefundRefundPsbtBuilder.buildRefundPsbt\` now also receives \`liveOutpoint\`. The service computes it from \`listOrderSweepsByOrderId\`, filtering to \`status='confirmed'\` and picking the most recent \`change_outpoint\`. Falls back to \`prefundFundedOutpoint\` when no confirmed sweeps exist. Pending/broadcast (but not yet confirmed) sweeps are intentionally excluded — they may not have landed on-chain, and the chain naturally resolves any race between refund and pending sweep (only one can spend the UTXO).

## L-PR-3 (medium-critical): no validation contract on cosignSweepPsbt

\`applyMakerSweepSignature\` trusts a maker-built PSBT and asks the \`OrderSweepSigner\` to add the desk's signature. A malicious maker could submit a PSBT that drains all the prefund grains to themselves — and the desk's co-sig would make it broadcastable.

**Fix:** documented the security contract on \`OrderSweepSigner.cosignSweepPsbt\`. Implementers MUST validate:
1. Exactly one input, matching \`sweep.inputOutpoint\`
2. Output 0 pays \`sweep.sweptGrains\` to the trade-escrow address
3. Output 1 (if present) pays change back to the prefund escrow address with the correct amount
4. No third output, no maker-pubkey spend-to-self
5. Fee within cap
6. nLockTime / nSequence allow the sweep leaf (not the maker_timeout_refund leaf)

The orchestrator only routes PSBTs; the implementer enforces the contract.

## Test results

383 tests pass / 0 fail. 6 new tests covering both fixes:
- L-PR-1: cancels funded order past CLTV (status → cancelled, state stays funded), before-CLTV leaves alone, idempotent on already-cancelled, scans both funded and partially_swept.
- L-PR-2: passes \`prefundFundedOutpoint\` when no sweeps; passes latest **confirmed** sweep's \`change_outpoint\` when sweeps exist (skipping pending ones).

body:
### What does this PR do?
Apply the `write_all` recipe documented at https://registry.bazel.build/docs/bazel_lib#lib-write_source_files-bzl: introduce `//pkg/proto/pbgo:write_all`, a single `write_source_files` umbrella that aggregates every `write_pb_go` and `go_mockgen` entry under `pkg/proto/pbgo/...`.
=> replace a dozen of sequential `bazel run` calls in `tasks/protobuf.generate` with one single invocation.

### Motivation
Each `bazel run` pays the client startup overhead.
Measured locally (with the legacy `msgp` regen still in place):
- before: ~9s
- after: ~6s (1.5x speedup)

This will be even more beneficial when `msgp` targets get fully `bazel`ified (2.2x speedup).

Another thing: it's possible to (re)generate the list of additional targets by means of a non-hermetic task, which I'll propose in a next PR.

### Describe how you validated your changes
- ran `dda inv protobuf.generate`: output identical to prior runs,
- timed both versions: warm cache, 10 samples each.

### Additional Notes
`write_pb_go` and `go_mockgen` now mark their generated `write_source_file(s)` as `visibility = ["//visibility:public"]` so the umbrella can reference them across package boundaries.
`visibility:public` is favored over something more granular for 2 reasons:
1. `write_pb_go` and `go_mockgen` are not tailored to `//pkg/proto/pbgo`. For instance, `write_pb_go` is used in `//pkg/security/proto/api`.
2. the `write_all` target is currenly sitting in `//pkg/proto/pbgo` but is likely to be extended/moved to the root BUILD.bazel file.

author: gharlan
body:
## Was & Warum

`NullAddon` wurde als Null-Object eingeführt, damit `Addon::get('foo')->isAvailable()` auch für nicht existierende Addons sicher aufrufbar ist. Mit dem Nullsafe-Operator ist das überflüssig:

```php
if (Addon::get('foo')?->isAvailable()) {}
```

Dazu kommt: Das Pattern wurde ohnehin schon inkonsistent gelebt — mehrere Caller (`AddonInstallCommand`, `AddonActivateCommand`, `AddonOperation` …) prüften bereits `instanceof Addon`, statt sich auf das Null-Object zu verlassen. `AddonInterface` wurde außerhalb von `Addon`/`NullAddon` von niemandem als Typehint oder für Polymorphie genutzt (Addons werden in 6.x per Subclass von `Addon` gebaut).

## Änderungen

- **Entfernt:** `Addon\AddonInterface` und `Addon\NullAddon`
- `Addon::get()` gibt jetzt `?Addon` zurück (`null` für unbekannte Addons) statt `AddonInterface`
- `Addon` implementiert kein Interface mehr; sinnvolle Typ-PHPDocs (`@return non-empty-string`, `@param non-empty-string`, `@see Config::*`) wurden auf die Klasse übernommen, reine Prosa weggelassen
- Caller auf `?->`, `Addon::require()` bzw. `null ===`-Checks umgestellt — Verhalten bleibt identisch
- `rector.php`: alte `rex_*_interface`/`rex_null_*`-Mappings zeigen jetzt auf `Addon\Addon`
- stale Psalm-Baseline-Eintrag für `NullAddon` entfernt

## BC-Hinweis

Breaking: `Addon\AddonInterface` und `Addon\NullAddon` existieren nicht mehr, `Addon::get()` kann `null` zurückgeben. Code muss von `Addon::get($x)->foo()` auf `Addon::get($x)?->foo()` umgestellt werden.

Checks: `composer cs` / PHPStan / Psalm grün.

## Summary

Adds three independently-configurable output filters to the transcript formatter so the LLM extraction can be cleaned, sanity-checked, and steered before downstream services persist it. Each filter can be toggled and re-tuned via env var or per-request metadata, so an operator can keep PII redaction on while disabling off-topic detection if it proves noisy — no redeploy required.

- **PII redaction** (`apply_pii_redaction`): blanks `caller_name` and `contact_info`, then scrubs phone numbers, emails, and any explicit mention of the caller's name (including first-name-only references) from the free-text fields.
- **Engineer review flag** (`evaluate_confidence_review`): sets `flagged_for_review` + `review_reasons` on the form when overall confidence is below the configured rank or too many fields are rated low.
- **Off-topic detection** (`detect_off_topic`): compares content-token overlap between the LLM output and the transcript. An off-topic initial response triggers a single clarifying retry through the existing ISR-297 retry plumbing. If the retry is also off-topic, the form keeps its structured data but is flagged for engineer review instead of going through the placeholder path.

Wiring:
- `forms.build_incident_form` runs PII redaction after the existing content filter, then computes the review decision after confidence extraction.
- `ollama_client._ai_fill_form` runs off-topic detection after each schema-valid response and reroutes the retry prompt accordingly.

Env vars (`OUTPUT_FILTER_*`) are documented in `.env.example`.

> Note: this branch was opened off `feature/isr-221-ai-output-reliability`, so until PR #19 (ISR-353) merges, this PR will also show the ISR-296–301 epic commits in its diff. The only ISR-355 commit here is the top one.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest transcript-formatter/tests/` — 23 unit tests passing (PII defaults, free-text scrubbing, name particle handling, metadata overrides, confidence thresholds, off-topic detection, cross-language overlap)
- [x] All four edited modules AST-parse cleanly
- [ ] Reviewer: confirm PII defaults are conservative enough for the SSM Repak use case
- [ ] Reviewer: confirm the off-topic 0.10 / 12-token defaults don't false-positive on short real calls

## Future work / related

- The pre-existing `content_filter._sanitize_text_value` uses `r"\\b...\\b"` (double-escaped backslashes), which is a literal backslash + `b` rather than a word boundary; out of scope here but worth a follow-up ticket.

body:
| Q              | A
| -------------- | ---
| Bug fix?       | no
| New feature?   | yes
| Deprecations?  | no
| Documentation? | no
| Issues         | -
| License        | MIT

Allow TwigComponent's runtime to work without `symfony/dependency-injection`.

`ComponentFactory` and `ComponentRuntime` only ever call `get()`/`has()` on
their injected service locator. Both methods are defined by PSR-11
`Psr\Container\ContainerInterface`, which Symfony's `ServiceLocator` already
implements — so the injection points can be typehinted against the interface
instead of the concrete class.

This decouples the runtime classes from the DI component: they can now be
wired with any PSR-11 container, enabling standalone (non-Symfony) usage with
just Twig. `symfony/dependency-injection` moves to `require-dev` (still pulled
transitively via `symfony/framework-bundle` in a full Symfony app, and only
needed at runtime for the bundle's extension/compiler-pass classes).

```php
// Standalone wiring, no symfony/dependency-injection required
$factory = new ComponentFactory(
    $templateFinder,
    $myPsr11Container, // any Psr\Container\ContainerInterface
    $propertyAccessor,
    $eventDispatcher,
    $config,
    $classMap,
    $twig,
);

body:
## Problem

PostHog team members sometimes commit with non-`@posthog.com` email addresses, which makes it harder to:
- Attribute commits to team members in internal tooling that keys off the `@posthog.com` address
- Distinguish team contributions from external community ones when scanning git history

This PR adds an automated nudge in the PR workflow to gently remind org members to use their PostHog email for commits.

## Changes

Added a new `check-author-email` job to `.github/workflows/pr-opened.yml` that:

1. **Verifies org membership** — Uses a GitHub App token to check if the PR author is an active PostHog org member (skips external contributors)
2. **Scans commit emails** — Examines all commits attributed to the PR author and flags any using non-`@posthog.com` addresses
3. **Posts a nudge comment** — If offending emails are found, posts a friendly comment once per PR with:
   - The non-PostHog email(s) detected
   - Explanation of why it matters
   - Git config commands to fix it locally or globally
   - Reassurance that no action is needed on the current PR

The job only runs on the initial `opened` action (not `ready_for_review`), fires exactly once per PR, and gracefully handles fork PRs where secrets aren't available.

## How did you test this code?

This is a CI workflow addition. The logic is straightforward:
- GitHub App token creation and org membership checks use standard GitHub Actions patterns
- Commit email detection uses the GitHub REST API's `pulls.listCommits` endpoint
- Comment deduplication uses a marker comment to prevent duplicate nudges
- Error handling is defensive (flaky membership lookups don't fail the PR, fork PRs are skipped)

The workflow will be tested in practice when merged and triggered by subsequent PRs from org members.

- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

author: renakaagusta
body:
## Summary

Adds a 5-minute in-process cache to `discoverPools()` in `tools/screening.js`. Within a single Node process (i.e., the meridian daemon), back-to-back calls within 5 minutes return the cached result instead of re-hitting the Meteora discovery API.

## Why

`discoverPools()` is the entry point for every screening cycle and for the dashboard's candidate refreshes. Each call:

- Fetches up to 50 pools from `pool-discovery-api.datapi.meteora.ag`
- Optionally batches Jupiter `assets/search` calls for deployer enrichment
- Filters / threshold-checks the result

p50 was ~4s for the wrapping `get_top_candidates`. The discovery leg itself is a ~300ms network call plus filtering, so the cache primarily pays off on rapid back-to-back screening — for example, the dashboard re-fetching after a config change, or multiple management/screening crons firing within the same 5-minute window.

## Behavior

- Cache TTL: **5 minutes**.
- Key: `(page_size, config.screening.timeframe, config.screening.category)` — different filter contexts get independent slots.
- New `bypassCache: true` arg on `discoverPools(...)` for callers that must have fresh data.
- New named export `invalidateDiscoveryCache()` for explicit busting (e.g., after a config change that affects filters).
- Cache is in-process / per Node runtime. Subprocess callers (e.g. an external agent framework that does `node cli.js candidates` per cycle) won't share state across invocations — each fresh process starts with an empty cache. A future PR could add a `~/.meridian/discovery-cache.json` layer for cross-process sharing if that becomes a need.

## Test plan

- `node --check tools/screening.js` → syntax OK.
- Two back-to-back `meridian candidates --limit 2` invocations in the same Node process (REPL) return the same `discoverPools` result without a second API call. Verified by inspecting `_discoveryCache` size after each call.
- The wrapping `get_top_candidates` still does fresh `getMyPositions` + per-pool enrichment — those are deliberately not cached because positions can change and enrichment data is volatile.

## Out of scope

- Caching `getTopCandidates` output (enriched + position-filtered). That cache would need to invalidate on every position open/close event; safer to leave as a future PR.
- File-based cross-process cache for subprocess callers.
- Caching `getPoolDetail`, `getTokenInfo`, etc. — same per-call cost as discovery and worth a follow-up.

- **28 spec files** generate 28 isolated clients (one per spec) under `src/<surface>/<spec-name>/`; `data-plane-signaling-api` is excluded (internal plane-to-plane comms not used by library consumers)

## Summary

Two product improvements that make rule-based categorization **transparent and safe to change**.

### Phase 1 — attribution & re-evaluation
Auto-categorization was a black box: you couldn't see which rule assigned a category, and editing/deleting a rule didn't reconcile the transactions it had touched.

- Track `Transaction.AppliedRuleId` — the rule that last auto-assigned the category (FK `SetNull`, + migration `AddTransactionAppliedRule`). Set on import and recategorize via the new `TransactionCategorizer.MatchRule` (returns the winning rule, not just its category); cleared on any manual edit / bulk-categorize.
- Transaction detail shows **"Zařazeno pravidlem „…""** (or "podle částky" for amount-only rules). `TransactionDto` carries `AppliedRuleId` + `AppliedRulePattern`.
- **Re-evaluation:** editing a rule re-checks the rows it had assigned (not only uncategorized ones); deleting a rule re-evaluates its rows against the remaining rules and clears those nothing else matches; restoring re-applies to uncategorized. Manual choices are never touched.

### Phase 2 — impact preview (dry-run)
- **"Náhled dopadu"** on the Rules page shows how many transactions a rule would match in its scope, how many already-categorized (non-manual) rows it would re-tag, and a few example transactions — before saving. Invaluable for regex / amount / family-wide rules.
- `POST /rules/preview` evaluates the unsaved rule (scope-restricted) with `MatchRule`; `RulePreviewDto` + API client + UI. No schema change.

## Tests
`MatchRule` returns the winning rule; full suite green (73). Migration applies cleanly; model in sync.

## Notes
Builds on the currency work in #37. Two further rule improvements (uncategorized triage, bulk management) are planned as follow-ups.

author: roryford
body:
Fixes two MLX lifecycle issues from a deep code review (#1498).

## 1. Arbiter teardown ordering vs a following load

`unloadModel()` (`MLXBackend.swift:570`) and `secureWipe()` (`:625`) spawned unstructured `Task { await MLXResourceArbiter.shared.release/clearAll(...) }` with no ordering guarantee. In the reload loop (`unloadModel()` → `loadModel()`), the new load's `arbiter.claim` (`:314`) could be enqueued on the arbiter **actor** *before* the prior `release` for the same `backendID` ran — the actor processes in scheduling order, not call order — silently dropping the fresh claim and leaving the reloaded model with a zero cache budget.

**Fix (chosen approach: chained `cleanupTask`, mirroring `LlamaBackend`):**
- Added a stored `_cleanupTask` (guarded by `stateLock`). Each `unloadModel`/`secureWipe` chains its `release`/`clearAll` onto the previous cleanup (`await previousCleanup?.value`) and stores the result back.
- `loadModel` awaits the pending cleanup (`await pendingCleanupTask()?.value`) *before* issuing its `claim`, so a stale teardown can never land after a fresh claim.
- Added `public func unloadAndWait() async` for the reload-loop / test path, mirroring `LlamaBackend.unloadAndWait()`.

The chained-task approach was chosen over a generation-token scheme because it exactly matches the established, proven `LlamaBackend.cleanupTask` pattern already in this codebase.

## 2. Stream `onTermination` only cancelled on `.cancelled`

`MLXBackend.swift:434-438` cancelled the generation task only on `.cancelled`. A consumer abandoning the stream early (deinit → `.finished`) left the `@MainActor` generation task running, occupying the GPU scheduler. Changed to `{ @Sendable _ in task.cancel() }` — cancel on **any** termination, matching Llama / Foundation / the SSE runner. The driver already treats `Task.isCancelled` as clean completion.

## Tests
Added `test_releaseBeforeClaim_barrierPreservesFreshClaim` to `MLXResourceArbiterTests` — a **Metal-free** regression test at the arbiter task-chain level. It proves that awaiting the chained `release` before `claim` preserves the fresh claim, and includes a control showing release-after-claim empties the table (the race the barrier averts).

## Test results
- `swift build --build-tests --traits MLX` — succeeds (Metal shader compile, ~107s).
- `swift test --traits MLX --filter MLXResourceArbiter` — 10/10 pass (incl. new test).
- `swift test --traits MLX --filter MLXBackend` — 87 executed, 13 skipped (Metal-gated via `XCTSkipIf`), 0 failures.

Closes #1498

author: martsokha
body:
## Summary

\`Tabular.row_index\` and \`Tabular.column_index\` were \`usize\`; \`ColumnHeader.column_index\` (in \`TabularMetadata.headers\`) was \`u32\`. Same semantic concept, two widths — every cell↔header join needed a cast.

\`u32\` is the right type for both. CSV / XLSX / SQL columns are bounded well below \`u32::MAX\`; \`usize\` was inherited from \`Vec::get\`'s parameter, not chosen for the data model.

Closes #218.

## Changes

**Public API (wire-breaking in theory)**
- \`Tabular::row_index: usize → u32\`
- \`Tabular::column_index: usize → u32\`
- \`Tabular::new(row: u32, col: u32)\` signature
- \`ColumnHeader::column_index\` unchanged (already \`u32\`)

**CSV handler internals**
- Cell construction: \`row_index as u32\` / \`col as u32\` at the \`enumerate()\` boundary.
- \`Vec::get\` lookups: \`location.column_index as usize\` at the call site.
- \`resolve_row\` accepts \`u32\` and returns \`(bool, usize)\` — the \`usize\` is correctly an index into the handler's \`Vec<Vec<String>>\`, so the cast belongs inside the helper.

**Engine**
- \`extraction/tabular.rs\` row-grouping \`BTreeMap<usize, _>\` → \`BTreeMap<u32, _>\`.
- \`detection/lift.rs\` cell passthrough unchanged (the source \`Tabular\` already carries \`u32\`).

**Tests**
- Two helpers (\`cell_with_offsets\`, \`cell_range\`) take \`u32\` row/col now.

## Wire impact

Theoretically wire-breaking if \`usize\` was serialized on a 64-bit target with a value above \`u32::MAX\`. In practice no real CSV / XLSX / SQL document has more than 4B columns, so persisted shapes never differ — wire-compatible-in-practice.

- Ghostscript `/ebook` exposed as a batch operation.
